title: Irregular galaxy NGC 55
caption: The irregular galaxy NGC 55, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This is NGC 55, an irregular galaxy photographed with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla Observatory in Chile. Unlike spirals or ellipticals, an irregular galaxy has no clear, orderly shape.

NGC 55 is about 7.5 million light-years away, which makes it a relatively close neighbor in galactic terms, and it measures some 70,000 light-years across. It lies in the southern constellation Sculptor.

The image was built from data taken through three filters. Two of them, called B and V, capture blue and yellow-green visible light, showing the galaxy's starlight. The third, H-alpha, isolates the red glow given off by hydrogen gas, and so highlights clouds where stars are forming. The field of view is 30 arcminutes wide, with north at the top and east to the left.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope, using B, V and H-alpha filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, which could not see this faint galaxy in such detail.
